Note on kinds: the disputed items use kinds template_unit_missed, identifier_missed and unstructured_unit_extra. These are not the kinds named in the brief. I used the kinds as they appear in disputed_items.json.

Per article:

1. en-1355140902: 1 confirmed, 0 corrected.
   - item 0 (template_unit_missed, cp 813): confirm. {{NRDB species}} is the whole body of ref RDB. It formats a citation to the Reptile Database, and the render reads "Heterodactylus lundii at the Reptarium.cz Reptile Database. Accessed 27 July 2019." That is a citation template under 3.1 ("purpose is to format a citation ... and similar"). The template is not named in the guide, so this rests on its purpose.

2. en-1377158630: 0 confirmed, 1 corrected.
   - item 0 (identifier_missed): correct. The locked identifier quotes the whole URL https://www.microbiologyresearch.org/content/journal/ijsem/10.1099/ijs.0.02401-0 at cp 2945. The 3.5 row quotes the whole URL only for a publisher URL whose path contains /doi/10., and this path has no /doi/ segment. So the "anything else" row applies and the raw text is the DOI itself. Corrected location: cp 3004, quote "10.1099/ijs.0.02401-0". Role identifier_link, key and notes are unchanged. The reading is ambiguous and is explained in the decision file.

3. en-1377880902: 3 confirmed, 1 corrected.
   - item 0 (cp 2357, note d2, "Not to be confused with..."): confirm. The note cites nothing, so unstructured stays false.
   - item 1 (cp 5568, note d3, "Of the 800,000 objects ... 737,000"): correct, unstructured false to true. The labelled link is the source of the figures, so the note cites a web source in plain text with no citation template. This is a borderline reading, since the link is labelled and not a bare URL.
   - item 2 (cp 5889, note d4, "NEO Rating"): confirm. The link explains a term and supports no claim, so it is a pointer and not a citation. Borderline.
   - item 3 (cp 6300, note d5, "The NEO Confirmation Page"): confirm. Same reasoning as item 2. Borderline.
